decisions.reason: The hypotheses permit M_a=-1, theta=1, A=I. On a bounded ball take u(x)=x_1, f=0, k=0 and a nonzero nonnegative smooth cutoff supported where x_1>0. This is a weak solution and S,b are positive, so the old step 1.1 bound of a nonnegative absolute cross term by 2M_a S b<0 is false. The energy estimate itself is sound: matrix Cauchy-Schwarz supplies sqrt(M_a^2)=|M_a|, and Young applied to S and |M_a|b yields the unchanged squared constants. Both offending factors were repaired in proof steps 1.1 and 2.1 and mirrored in the owning contract.

reviews.reason: Reviewed the full assigned claim, Facts and three proof steps, its owning contract and page, current prerequisite statements, the truncation proof, positive-cone density argument and explicit bump construction. Compact support and local L2 forcing license the nonnegative Sobolev test for every real level. Symmetric positive-definite A gives matrix Cauchy-Schwarz, then Holder bounds the cross term by 2|M_a|S b. Young absorbs half S^2 and ellipticity gives exactly 4M_a^2/theta and 2/theta. The radial bump derivative is at most 4||sigma prime||_infinity/(R-r); the ball estimate follows with the stated uniform constants. Zero energy and empty superlevel sets require no division; all declared choice assumptions are retained. Exactly two proof factors changed; the Statement is byte-identical, so there is no downstream interface event. This is the repair author mathematical review, not an independent audit.
